page: Amazon Web Services c8id.96xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors on the x86_64 architecture. It features 384 vCPUs, consisting of 192 physical cores with hyper-threading, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor configuration includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of 22,800 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and network connectivity is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps under the Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the c8id.96xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core tests, PassMark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The memory subsystem delivers top-tier read and write bandwidths for both small cached and large uncached blocks. The server also excels in specialized compute workloads, achieving top-tier results in software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and cryptographic execution. Database operations and Redis SET operations similarly rank in the top 10% of tested systems, supported by the high-throughput local NVMe storage.

Tradeoffs are present in single-core and specific inference workloads. Single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the average and strong categories, respectively, rather than the top tier. Furthermore, while prompt processing for medium and large language models is strong, text generation speeds for small models register in the bottom 10%. Given these performance characteristics, the server is highly efficient for parallelized compute tasks, high-throughput database deployments, static web serving, and intensive compilation workloads, while being less suited for single-threaded applications or dedicated GPU-accelerated tasks.
